newsitem.title: UK: UK's Capital to buy Branson's Virgin Radio.
newsitem.headline: UK's Capital to buy Branson's Virgin Radio.

text.p: Britain's Capital Radio Plc will gain a key national licence through the acquisition of Richard Branson's Virgin Radio in a 65 million pound ($105 million) deal, Capital said on Tuesday.

Branson, whose Virgin empire spans airlines to insurance, is to become a non-executive director of Capital under the all-paper deal. Virgin interests will control some 14 percent of the enlarged company.
The two companies said that the merger would create a strong commercial force to develop digital radio, which is expected to offer CD-quality sound when it hits the airwaves in 1999.

"The merging of our radio businesses creates a new force in British commercial radio with the resources to commit to a digital future and mount a concerted challenge to the BBC's domination of this new technology," bearded entrepreneur Branson said in a statement.
One of Britain's leading commercial radio operators, Capital has expanded beyond its London base in recent years, acquiring stations in Birmingham and a number of southern English counties.

Virgin Radio, set up four years ago, has one London FM rock music licence in addition to its national AM contemporary music radio licence. Crucially it has been guaranteed a digital licence for its national service.
"The acquisition of Virgin Radio is based on strong commercial logic and fits superbly into the group's long term strategy of building a music entertainment group," said Capital chairman Ian Irvine.

On Tuesday Capital announced pre-tax profit of 17 million pounds, up nine percent, in the six months to end-March. The company recently moved into the restaurant business, acquiring the "My Kinda Town" chain.
Commercial radio has been a growth business in Britain over the past decade, the number of stations mushrooming from 45 to over 200. Virgin 1215 is one of only three national commercial stations.

The deal is conditional on regulatory approval but Capital said it believed its ownership would not infringe the terms of new broadcasting legislation. It said it would aim to ensure that Virgin FM's output would not duplicate that of its core Capital FM rock music station.
